# manage_dynamic_function_tool

> CRUD operations for serverless JavaScript functions with scheduling and OAuth support.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | `dynamic_functions` |
| Callable | MCP clients; in-app @ai conversations; grantable to agents |
| Filter | `https://www.dsiloed.com/api/v1/mcp?tools=manage_dynamic_function_tool` |

## Description

This is the description the server sends to the model, verbatim.

CRUD operations for serverless JavaScript functions with scheduling and OAuth support.

ACTIONS: create, update, delete

REQUIRED FOR CREATE: name (1-128 chars, alphanumeric/_/-), javascript_code
OPTIONAL: description, active (default: true), schedule (cron), timeout_seconds (1-300, default: 30),
          configuration (JSON), shared_configuration_id, callback_model, callback_event, callback_async, run_as_user_id

IMPORTANT: run_as_user_id is REQUIRED for scheduled or callback functions. This specifies which user's
permissions are used when the function executes in the background. Use current_user (special value) to
automatically use the user making the request.

JS CONTEXT: params, config, functionId, functionName, tenantId, configurations, oauth (see below)

SANDBOX DIALECT — READ BEFORE WRITING CODE. V8 via mini_racer: not Node, not a
browser, and with no real I/O every helper is SYNCHRONOUS.
  * `await` IS supported, including at top level, and so is `async`. Awaiting a
    synchronous helper simply yields its value, so `await fetch(url)` works.
  * fetch() returns the response ITSELF, not a Promise, so there is no .then():
    `fetch(url).then(...)` throws "fetch(...).then is not a function".
    Correct: var r = fetch(url, {headers: {...}}); if (!r.ok) { ... }
             var body = r.json();   // also r.text(), r.status, r.body
  * `oauth` is UNDEFINED (not null) until the connection is authorised, so a
    bare reference throws ReferenceError. Always guard:
    if (typeof oauth === 'undefined' || !oauth || !oauth.accessToken) { ... }
    Auth header: {'Authorization': (oauth.tokenType || 'Bearer') + ' ' + oauth.accessToken}
  * Return with a top-level `return {...}` OR by ending on a bare expression
    `({...})`. Returning nothing yields {} — an empty result means the code ran
    fine and produced no value, NOT that it failed.

  * HELPERS are POSITIONAL unless they search/update: readFile(fileId),
    sendMessage(conversationId, message, options), sendEmail(toEmail, subject,
    emailBody, fromEmail), addConversationMember(conversationId, partyId, admin);
    listFiles({directory_path, type, limit, offset}) pages at 20 by default and
    returns {data, total_count} — loop on offset; updateFile(fileId, {...}).
    readFile returns full_text for a document with extracted text, content otherwise.
  * RESULT SIZE: the caller sees your return value through a tool result capped at
    15,000 characters; anything larger is delivered paged (result_truncated: true).
    Return compact keys, cap lists, or a summary plus a createFile() for bulk.

Test the FIRST version before rewriting it: the error names the one thing to
fix, and guessing twice costs more than running once.

CALLBACK MODELS: Party, Individual, Organization, Project, Task, TimeEntry, Timesheet, BizTxnEvent, BizTxnAccount, User, Tenant, TenantSignup
CALLBACK EVENTS: create, update, destroy, all
Callback params: {event, model_name, record_id, record, timestamp, changes (update), destroyed (destroy)}

SHARED CONFIG: Reference a Configuration by ID or internal_identifier for OAuth across functions.
OAuth config structure: {oauth: {provider, client_id, client_secret, authorize_url, token_url, scopes}}

EXAMPLES:
Create: {action: "create", name: "hello", javascript_code: "return {msg: 'Hi ' + params.name};"}
Scheduled: {action: "create", name: "daily_sync", javascript_code: "...", schedule: "0 9 * * *", run_as_user_id: "current_user"}
Callback: {action: "create", name: "on_party", callback_model: "Party", callback_event: "create", javascript_code: "...", run_as_user_id: 123}
Update: {action: "update", name: "hello", active: false}
Delete: {action: "delete", name: "hello"}

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | string | yes | Action: create, update, delete. |
| `id` | integer | no | Function ID (for update/delete - can use id OR name) |
| `name` | string | no | Function name (required for create, can also be used for update/delete to find function) |
| `new_name` | string | no | New function name (for renaming a function during update) |
| `description` | string | no | Function description. |
| `javascript_code` | string | no | JavaScript code to execute. |
| `active` | boolean | no | Whether function is active. |
| `schedule` | string | no | Cron expression for scheduling. |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | no | Max execution time (1-300) |
| `configuration` | object | no | Custom configuration object. Any key that looks like a secret (api_key, *_token, password, credentials, etc.) is stored encrypted and REMOVED from the plain configuration entirely — it will not appear in a later get/manage response at all. The response's configuration_keys lists every key that was actually saved, secret or not, by name only, so a saved secret does not look like a silent failure. |
| `shared_configuration_id` | string \| integer | no | ID or internal_identifier of a Configuration record to share across functions (set to null to remove) |
| `callback_model` | string | no | Model to trigger callback on. Valid values: Party, Individual, Organization, Project, Task, TimeEntry, Timesheet, BizTxnEvent, BizTxnAccount, User, Tenant, TenantSignup. |
| `callback_event` | string | no | Event to trigger callback on: create, update, destroy, or all. |
| `callback_async` | boolean | no | Run this callback in the BACKGROUND (default false = inline, blocking the request that triggered it). Set true for slow work — opening conversations, invoking an agent, calling out to a third party — so the triggering request is not held open. Per FUNCTION, not per model. |
| `run_as_user_id` | string \| integer | no | User ID to execute as for scheduled/callback functions. REQUIRED for scheduled or callback functions. Use "current_user" to automatically use the user making the request. |
